description: Eight shift registers of random bits, each looping as its own sequence with a trigger and a stepped voltage

params.text: Sets what happens to the bit entering that track's register on each clock: centred makes it random, fully clockwise locks the loop, and moving left of centre doubles the loop length
Sets how many steps that track's loop runs, up to 16, and up to 32 with its CTRL knob left of centre
Attenuates that track's CV output, 0% to 100%
Adds a fixed voltage to that track's CV output, -10V to +10V

inputs.text: Advances that track's register one step on each trigger
A trigger here restarts that track's sequence from its beginning
Moves that track's CTRL setting, added to its CTRL knob

outputs.text: A 1ms pulse each time that track advances onto an on bit, or a gate or a clock-width pulse under Output TRG type; the bottom one can carry all eight tracks as a polyphonic cable instead
The voltage built from the on bits of that track's register, attenuated and offset; the bottom one can carry all eight tracks as a polyphonic cable instead

notes: every bit off gives 0V and every bit on gives 10V before the SCL and OFS knobs; each bit position is worth a different amount, doubling as you go by default.
this version has no DEL, ADD, RND or CLR controls and no stored patterns; each track is shaped by its CTRL knob alone.
menu: Math Settings — a submenu holding Bit Resolution and Voltage progression
Bit Resolution: 8 bit, 16 bit — sets how many of each register's bits the output voltage is built from
Voltage progression: 2x (std.), 1.3x, Fibonacci — sets how much each further bit is worth in the output voltage
Output TRG type: Trig, Gate, Clock Width — chooses whether an on bit sends a 1ms pulse, a gate held until an off bit, or a pulse the length of the incoming clock's high part
Polyphony on 8th out: Monophonic, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 — sets how many tracks the bottom pair of outputs gathers into one polyphonic cable each
Don't advance — makes the first clock after a reset hold on the first step rather than moving off it
Copy All Tracks — puts all eight sequences on a clipboard
Paste All Tracks — takes all eight sequences off that clipboard
Copy track — a submenu of Copy Track 1 to Copy Track 8, which puts one sequence on a clipboard
Paste to track — a submenu of Paste Track 1 to Paste Track 8, which writes the copied sequence over the one you pick
DISK operations — a submenu with Load Preset and Save Preset for the whole module, and Import trigSeq seq. to: and Export trigSeq seq. from: for one track at a time
Clear ALL Sequences — turns every bit of every track off
Initialize on Start — clears the registers when Rack loads a patch
